doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

title: The 'Americana Suite' premiere in Aachen
summary: He describes flying to Aachen where Ralf Kemper arranged for the symphony and conductor Christopher Ward to perform his Americana Suite, his first time hearing another conductor lead his work.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And what’s it like for other people to conduct your work?
Well funny you should mention it. You see this?

I wrote a huge orchestral piece over the course of another twenty-something years and I came up with one more piece about a year ago that I spent a lot of time on. And I called it the “Americana Suite” because it has a lot of connections with my youth and blah-blah and you know adventures. And Ralf Kemper called the conductor of the Aachen, Germany symphony orchestra, Aachen, for anybody’s information is the home of, was the home of Charlemagne so he’s got a symphony orchestra. And the conductor said yes, so in February I got my fly miles and flew over there and they performed this. They had like four rehearsals and it was recorded at the time of the pandemic but performed about a year later. And that was an answer to your question —
About your expectations of your piece when someone else is conducting it?

That’s right. Yeah this was my first experience. And the conductor, a wonderful English conductor, Christopher Ward, he also conducts the Memphis Orchestra I think, he took it upon himself and conducted — oh man — it was just a wonderful thing to see. So I’m sorry to go on but it’s like yes, somebody believing in music that I believed in. It’s not commercial stuff you know, it’s not high art but it’s my best attempt and to see somebody like on a court going like that or cuing this and it’s all visceral to me because I know what he’s doing and he’s getting results you know. So that’s a wonderful feeling, especially because now when I orchestrate something I know that that’s what I need you © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

know, and there it is. And it says it on paper there with my pencil that went into the computer. So that’s a joyous feeling. And the other thing too is the German audiences, they’re a different kind of animal. I mean I was sitting to the side discreetly just observing the symphony playing and a lot of the audience was sitting on the edge of their seats like listening, you know, attentively. It’s like woo! So it’s yeah, that’s a whole experience in music, and that’s why the boy got on the boat I guess is because what people do to me, what Bird did to me, what Bud in my own little reflective life I’d like to do something to somebody else.
